newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to defend settlements at White House.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to defend settlements at White House.

text.p: Israel's leader Benjamin Netanyahu will insist when he meets U.S. President Bill Clinton on Monday that the Jewish state has a right to go on building Jewish settlements, an Israeli spokesman said on Thursday.

"The prime minister will make clear in Washington that Israel stands by its right to build in Jerusalem and in settlements, and included in that the building will continue at Har Homa," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said.

Israeli-Palestinian relations were plunged into two weeks of crisis and clashes after Netanyahu broke ground on Har Homa, a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on a hilltop Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

"From Israel's standpoint, the purpose of the prime minister's trip to Washington is to strengthen the understanding that a basic condition of the peace process is that the Palestinian Authority keep its commitment to fight terrorism," Bazak said in the statement.
"Only after that will be made clear, will it be possible to clarify how to make progress in the peace process, including by way of the initiatives that the prime minister raised."

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it, claiming it was part of Israel's eternal capital. Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent state.
